findings.title: Team admin check requires both admin and owner, so admins are denied
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. A user must be both a team admin and a team owner to pass. A plain team admin, or a plain owner, who is not also the other role is rejected with FORBIDDEN. The intended check is almost certainly `||`. Team admins and owners who are not the organizer cannot add guests as the feature intends.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive while the blacklist is lowercased
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71), but the incoming `guest` is compared as-is (line 77: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). An email such as `Spam@Example.com` will not match a blacklisted `spam@example.com`, so blacklisted addresses can be added by changing case. Emails should be normalized (lowercased) before both the blacklist check and the duplicate check.

findings.title: Duplicate emails within one request are not removed before insert
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails that already exist as attendees and blacklisted addresses. It does not deduplicate the `guests` array itself. A request containing the same address twice (or differing only by case) will create two attendee rows via `createMany`, and the calendar and email fan-out will also double up. The dialog validates uniqueness, but the API does not enforce it.

findings.title: Database write happens before calendar update with no rollback
findings.body: The attendees are persisted with `prisma.booking.update` (line 92) before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs (line 165). If the calendar update throws, the guests remain in the database but are missing from the calendar, and the caller gets an error. A retry then filters those guests out as existing attendees and returns BAD_REQUEST `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading and leaves the calendar permanently out of sync.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed with no error details logged
findings.body: The catch block logs only the static string "Error sending AddGuestsEmails" and discards the `err` object, so the actual failure cause is lost. It should log the error (e.g. via the project logger with the error and booking id).

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type metadata
findings.body: Every other send function in this file gates host and attendee emails with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` and accepts `eventTypeMetadata` or the disable flags. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no such parameter and always emails the organizer, team members and attendees. Organizers who disabled standard emails for the event type will still receive these notifications.

findings.title: Fallback error message is unreachable
findings.body: `message` is built as a template string containing `err.data?.code` and `t(err.message)`, so it is always truthy. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never runs, and the toast will show something like `undefined: ...` when `err.data` is missing. The fallback logic should check the raw values before interpolation.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip text bypasses i18n
findings.body: The tooltip content `"Remove email"` is a literal string, while every other user-facing label in this component and the dialog goes through `t()`. Non-English users will see English text, and the component already has `useLocale` available.

findings.title: Label references an id that is not present in the DOM
findings.body: The `<label htmlFor="emails">` points to an element id `emails` that is never rendered, so the label is not associated with any input. Screen readers and label-click behaviour are therefore broken for this field.

findings.title: No limit on number of guests or input normalization
findings.body: `guests` is an unbounded array of emails with no max length, and emails are not trimmed or lowercased at the schema level. This allows arbitrarily large requests that each trigger calendar updates and one email per attendee, and it is the root cause of the case-sensitivity and duplicate issues above.
